land.text: Equatoria south of the Mahdist front: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan with Wadelai near Lake Albert (the Egyptian province also took in northern Uganda, Lake Albert and West Nile)

predecessors.note: Equatoria had been a province of the Egyptian Sudan since 1870; the Mahdists had cut it off by 1883 and in 1885 Emin withdrew south to Wadelai.

land.text: Equatoria (the three Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Wadelai reach), taken by the Mahdist State in 1889 according to the Mahdist State dossier

successors.note: The Mahdist State page says "The Belgians prevented the Mahdi's men from conquering Equatoria": the handover is uncertain.

capitals.name: Wadelai
capitals.note: "In 1885, Emin and most of his forces withdrew further south, to Wadelai near Lake Albert." Coordinates approximate; the page names Lado as Emin's base after 1876 and Dufile as the place of the 1888 mutiny.

rulers.name: Emin Pasha (Mehemet Emin), governor
rulers.title: governor with the title Bey
rulers.note: Appointed in 1878; the Equatoria page says he was deposed by his officers in August 1887, the Emin Pasha page has a mutiny from August to November 1888 with Emin imprisoned at Dufile and Stanley meeting him in April 1888.

correction.text: Equatoria south of the Mahdist front: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan with Wadelai near Lake Albert (the Egyptian province also took in northern Uganda, Lake Albert and West Nile)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, corrected after review. The first draft used the gazetteer region 'Equatoria', which resolves to the whole of South Sudan (about 0.64 M km2, Bahr el Ghazal and Upper Nile included): a factor of about 3.4 over the Equatoria page's infobox 195,847.67 km2 (no year given; the infobox is for the modern Equatoria region). The page says Bahr el Ghazal "was split from Equatoria in 1948", so it was never part of the 1870-1889 core drawn here, and that the province "also contained most of northern parts of present-day Uganda, including Lake Albert and West Nile". Now drawn as admin-1 Central, Eastern and Western Equatoria (about 192,000 km2 on the gazetteer grid, matching the infobox) plus a 120 km disc at Wadelai (the Emin Pasha page: "In 1885, Emin and most of his forces withdrew further south, to Wadelai near Lake Albert"), about 0.233 M km2 with the disc (grid figure), a ratio of 1.19 to the infobox. West Nile is covered only by the disc: the gazetteer has no West Nile admin-1.

ledger.note: 1885: Emin Pasha, cut off from Khartoum, withdraws to Wadelai. "In 1885, Emin and most of his forces withdrew further south, to Wadelai near Lake Albert"; "The revolt of Muhammad Ahmad that began in 1881 had cut Equatoria off from the outside world by 1883."

region.text: Equatoria south of the Mahdist front: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan with Wadelai near Lake Albert (the Egyptian province also took in northern Uganda, Lake Albert and West Nile)

ledger.note: 1889: the Egyptian outpost ends and the Mahdists take the province. "The Mahdist Revolt put an end to Equatoria as an Egyptian outpost in 1889." The page also says that after Emin's Advance reached the coast "the Mahdists were firmly in control of Equatoria" (it gives no year for this; the Advance is dated by the page to a February 1887 start and arrival "by the end of the year"). The Mahdist State page, read in the first run, says the Belgians prevented the Mahdi's men from conquering Equatoria, so the day-to-day extent of Mahdist control is uncertain; the year 1889 is the Equatoria page's. The Mahdist State dossier of af-01-c records a 1889 gain with the counterpart string 'Equatoria Province', which this dossier takes over.

region.text: Equatoria as held in 1885-1889: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Wadelai reach

ledger.note: 1889: Equatoria ends as an Egyptian outpost; Emin's men stayed near Lake Albert until 1890, when Lugard took them to Kampala Hill, and Stanley and Emin reached Bagamoyo in 1890 (Emin Pasha page).

wars.name: Mahdist War (Equatoria front)

zones.text: Equatoria as held in 1885-1889: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Wadelai reach

wars.outcome: Equatoria cut off from 1883, Emin and his garrisons isolated; a British expedition reached Emin in 1886-1889 and he left; the Egyptian outpost ended in 1889.
wars.note: The Mahdist War page gives no date for the loss of Equatoria and names no Mahdist conquest of it.

certainty.note: A string of garrisons around the Nile and Lake Albert; no frontier is described.

sources.title: Equatoria
sources.note: Established 1870, extent (northern Uganda, Lake Albert, West Nile), Mahdist cut-off 1883, Emin deposed August 1887, end as an Egyptian outpost 1889.

sources.title: Emin Pasha
sources.note: Appointed governor 1878; cut off by 1883; withdrew to Wadelai in 1885; mutiny August-November 1888; arrived at Bagamoyo 1890.

sources.title: Mahdist War
sources.note: Equatoria 1886-1889: a British expedition reached Emin Pasha; no date for a loss of Equatoria.

notes:
New dossier, type colony: the remnant of the Egyptian province of Equatoria (made in 1870) after the fall of Khartoum, 1885-1889, split from turco-egyptian-sudan. Pages opened: Equatoria, Emin Pasha, Mahdist War (3). Disagreements: the Equatoria page says Emin was deposed by his officers in August 1887, the Emin Pasha page has a mutiny August-November 1888; the Equatoria page ends the outpost in 1889, the Emin Pasha page has Stanley and Emin at Bagamoyo in 1890. The Equatoria page does say "the Mahdists were firmly in control of Equatoria" after Emin left (no year); the Mahdist State page says the Belgians prevented the Mahdi's men from conquering it, so the extent of Mahdist control is uncertain; the Lado Enclave (1894-1910) is not on the Equatoria page. Counterpart for the end is mahdist-state at confidence 1 to agree with the af-01-c dossier; if a gap-filler finds the land went to nobody (or to the Congo Free State, Britain/Uganda), change both.
Uganda: the Egyptian province took in northern Uganda (Lake Albert, West Nile); the gazetteer has no 'West Nile' admin1, so a 120 km radius at Wadelai stands in. Gazetteer names needed: Wadelai (place, about 2.74 N 31.47 E, Nile near Lake Albert, northwestern Uganda).
Review repair (2026-10-19): the shape was redrawn from the gazetteer region 'Equatoria' (all of South Sudan, 0.64 M km2) to admin-1 Central, Eastern and Western Equatoria plus the Wadelai disc (about 0.233 M km2 on the grid against the infobox 195,848 km2; the three states alone are 192,000 km2); ledger/1 raised to confidence 2 with the page's sentence quoted.
